_about: The games the capture rig supports. One entry per game; adding a game is an entry here plus a profile in rig/profiles. steamAppId / epicAppName / installRegistryKey with installRegistryValue (a registry value holding the install folder, for a game another launcher installs) / xboxFolder (the game's folder in an Xbox app library, XboxGames/<xboxFolder>/Content) / folder (a folder the game always lives in, %VARIABLES% expanded: Minecraft's .minecraft) let the app find an install by itself; otherwise the user browses to the game's folder. exeDir is the folder holding the *-Win64-Shipping.exe, relative to the install; leave it empty to search for it. exe names the game's exe when it is not *-Win64-Shipping.exe. ue4ss names the UE4SS zip in redist/ the game needs (default UE4SS_v3.0.1.zip), ue4ssHooks the only UE4SS hooks left on for an engine the others do not fit; files the game's UE4SS needs beside it go in rig/unreal/games/<id>/. engineMajor/engineMinor force UE4SS's engine version, only for games whose scan fails without it. launch names what Launch game starts when it is not the store's own way: a link (steam://, shell:AppsFolder\...) or an exe in the game's folder. gameVersion (Minecraft) is the game version the rig's mod is built for.

games.name: The Ascent
games.notes: Built and measured on this game. Six cameras of 1024 px hold 30 volumes a second on an RTX 3060 Ti in DX12.

games.name: Risk of Rain 2
games.notes: Unity, through BepInEx 5. Five 512 px cameras hold 30 volumes a second on an RTX 3060 Ti. The game's own Frame Rate Limit caps it too: raise it if it is set to 30.

games.name: Mortal Kombat 1
games.notes: Offline modes only (Practice, Towers, the tutorial): stay out of online play while the rig is installed. The volume follows the middle of the two fighters. NetherRealm's engine fork needs a newer UE4SS, with one hook, and a vtable layout of its own; the installer brings both.

games.name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
games.notes: The rig hooks the game's renderer and renders the world again from each face of the cube in the same frame as the player's view: about 40 complete cubes a second with four faces on an RTX 3060 Ti, and the player keeps the controls and sees every frame. Uncap the frame rate. Turn off anti-aliasing, sharpening, motion blur, blur, depth of field, frame generation and dynamic resolution. The HUD stays on: the rig keeps it out of the faces. A script mod: another mod that replaces the player script must be merged with it first.

games.name: Cyberpunk 2077
games.notes: The game's own render-to-texture cameras - the kind holocalls use - five of them on V, rendered in the same frame as the player's view: 30 complete cubes a second with five faces of 512 px on an RTX 3060 Ti, the game at about 63 frames a second, the player's controls, frames and HUD untouched. The installer adds Cyber Engine Tweaks, RED4ext and Codeware unless the game has them already. After installing, load a save once: the cameras go on V as she is loaded.

games.name: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order
games.notes: Unreal Engine 4.21, single player, third person: five faces of 512 px at 30 volumes a second, the game at 60 frames a second. The Epic Games Store copy is installed and started by the EA app, which keeps its folder in the registry; Steam's is found as usual.

games.name: Star Wars Battlefront II (2017)
games.notes: Frostbite, no rig module: the add-on adds the cube's faces to the engine's own list of views, and the engine draws them in the same frame as yours - three faces at most (the first three ticked). The volume stands on your soldier's feet. Turn the faces on with F7 once in play. Play offline only: the campaign or Arcade. Keep DirectX 12 off in the game's settings.

games.name: The Sims 4
games.notes: No rig module: the add-on has the game's own renderer draw the lot again from each face's camera, in the same frame as yours. The volume follows the game's camera: the ground it looks at stays at the height the feet are set to, and the volume turns as the camera does. The faces are drawn in a lot, not in the menus. F7 stops and starts them. Keep the game on DirectX 11 (its default).

games.name: Crysis
games.notes: The 2007 original, patch 1.2.1, not Remastered. No rig module: the add-on has the game's own 3D engine draw the world again from each face's camera, in the same frame as yours. The volume stands on your feet and turns as you look round. F7 stops and starts the faces. On a current PC the game itself often will not start (it hangs or crashes before its menu, with or without the rig): the community's c1-launcher (github.com/ccomrade/c1-launcher) fixes that - download it yourself and start the game with it. Use the 64-bit DirectX 10 game. For the EA app or Xbox app copy, use Set folder... and pick the Crysis folder's Bin64. Launch game starts it through c1-launcher (CrysisC1.exe in Bin64).

games.name: Gang Beasts
games.notes: Unity IL2CPP, through BepInEx 6, which the installer brings. The first start after installing takes a minute or two longer: BepInEx builds the game's interop assemblies once, and downloads Unity's libraries for that, so be online for it. The volume follows the first beast played on this PC. Local games only: stay out of online play while the rig is installed. The Xbox app (PC Game Pass) copy is found by itself.

games.name: Totally Accurate Battle Simulator
games.notes: Unity (Mono), through BepInEx 5. The volume holds what the game's camera looks at, like a tabletop, and moves, grows and turns with the camera as you pan, zoom and orbit; hold Page Up or Page Down in the game to take in more or less on top of that. Campaign and sandbox only: stay out of online battles while the rig is installed. The Xbox app (PC Game Pass) copy is found by itself.

games.name: Cities: Skylines II
games.notes: Unity (Mono) with Unity's high-definition renderer, through BepInEx 5. Not working yet: being probed. The Xbox app (PC Game Pass) copy is found by itself.

games.name: F1 2020
games.notes: Codemasters' EGO engine. No rig module: the add-on puts its cameras into the game's own reflection cubemap, whose six views the engine draws in the same frame as yours. Start the DirectX 12 game (F1_2020_dx12.exe; Steam's launch options) and set Graphics Options, Advanced Setup, Vehicle Reflections to Ultra High: that turns the cubemap on. The Showroom works. In a race the volume follows your car, but the game leaves your own car out of its cubemap, so the volume shows the track and the other cars round it. The car's paint reflects the rig's views while the rig is on. Offline modes only (Grand Prix, Time Trial, career): stay out of online races while the rig is installed. The DirectX 11 game crashes on some PCs as a race loads, with or without the rig.

games.name: Minecraft Dungeons II
games.notes: Unreal 5.6. The game's code is protected, so the rig comes in as a Blueprint Loader mod: get Blueprint Loader from Nexus Mods (Minecraft Dungeons II, Blueprint Loader) and put its BlueprintLoader folder in the game's Dungeons\Content\Paks\~mods folder (make ~mods if it is not there) before Install rig. The volume stands on your hero's feet; Player look covers your hero and the mobs. The mod reads the app's settings twice a second, so changes take half a second. Offline play only: stay out of online games while the rig is installed. The Xbox app (PC Game Pass) copy is found by itself.

games.name: Undisputed
games.notes: Unity IL2CPP with Unity's high-definition renderer, through BepInEx 6, which the installer brings. The first start after installing takes a minute or two longer: BepInEx builds the game's interop assemblies once, and downloads Unity's libraries for that, so be online for it. The volume stands between the two boxers and turns with the game's camera. Offline fights only: stay out of online play while the rig is installed. The Xbox app (PC Game Pass) copy is found by itself.

games.name: Minecraft: Java Edition
games.notes: Version 26.3, through Fabric Loader, which you install first: get the Fabric installer from fabricmc.net, choose Minecraft 26.3 and Install, then Install rig here. The rig is a Fabric mod in .minecraft\mods: the game draws each face once more in every frame, and a small program beside it (voxon_capture_mc.exe, which the mod starts) turns them into volumes. Launch game opens the Minecraft Launcher: choose the fabric-loader 26.3 installation and press Play. The volume stands on your feet and turns with your view. Single-player worlds only: stay off servers and Realms while the rig is installed.

games.name: Black Myth: Wukong
games.notes: UE5. Every camera is a full UE5 lit render, so it starts at 15 captures a second.

games.name: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered
games.notes: UE5 over Gamebryo. Third person reads best.

games.name: Sifu
games.notes: Epic Games Store.

games.name: Mothergunship
games.notes: Epic Games Store. A first-person shooter: better watched than played from the volume.

games.name: Train Sim World 2
games.notes: Epic Games Store. A train wants a long window: 25 m to start.

games.name: Unreal Tournament (pre-alpha)
games.notes: Epic Games Store. Bots and LAN only.
